about: Results of the AI editorial review for articles published with the automated label. Not a person's review.

entries.notes: Every record checked against its source on 2026-10-02: NBA.com Top Moments pages (Warriors 2015-16: 24-0 start beating the 15-0 shared by the 1948-49 Capitols and 1993-94 Rockets, 73 wins, lost 2016 Finals; Bulls 1995-96: 72-10 .878, broke the Lakers' 69-13 .841, won the title); NBA.com best-starts list (Nov 2024: 24-0, then 15-0 x3); NBA.com 33-game streak page (5 Nov 1971 to 7 Jan 1972, ended by Milwaukee two nights later; 69-13); Basketball-Reference 1971-72 Lakers schedule (W33 at Atlanta 7 Jan, L at Milwaukee 9 Jan 1972) and 2024-25 Cavaliers schedule (15-0, L at Boston 19 Nov 2024); NBA.com 1967-68 review (Seattle and San Diego added, quote 'now a 12-team league, played its first 82-game schedule' verbatim); Basketball-Reference 1966-67 summary (10 teams, every W+L = 81); 1998-99 review (3 months lost, February start, 50 games, quote verbatim); 2011-12 review (lockout from 30 June 2011, 149 days, 66 games, Christmas Day); NBA.com 2020 suspension story (Wednesday 11 March 2020, preliminary positive test); NBA PR 17 Nov 2020 (72 games from 22 Dec); NBA PR 2026-27 schedule (opens Tue 20 Oct; 'NBA's 81st regular season'; 80 of 82 games fixed, two set by Cup Group Play, 4-10 Dec); NBA Cup 101 (Championship 'will not be counted as a regular-season game' verbatim); NCAA.com Feb 2026 history (7 unbeaten champions, last Indiana 1975-76 32-0; Gonzaga 24-0 in 2021 lost the final). Also checked that nothing since changes the record book: 2025-26 best record 64-18 and best opening run 8-0 (Basketball-Reference 2026 standings and Oct-Nov 2025 schedules). Recomputed every figure: .890/.878/.841; p=73/82: p^24 = 6.1% (1 in 16), p^82 = 0.0072% (1 in 13,812), 0.5^(1/82) = 99.16%, p^32 = 2.4%; 24/82 < 1/3. Edits: best-starts sentence now says Cleveland was still unbeaten when the NBA.com list was published and lost its 16th game (added the two Basketball-Reference schedules as sources); takeaway's '89% chance' made '73-in-82 (89%)' because 0.89 exactly gives 1 in 14,100; cut the unsupported claim that the question 'comes up most often' from management-game players and that seasons simulate 'in minutes'. Teams named only for cited records; no athletes named; no affiliation implied. App claims match dump-catalog (GM app: draft from a pool, 82-game season, playoff race; pool from real players' careers with the game's own ratings per content-spec rule 10, never called fictional; Career Sim: awards, records, legacy score, fictional). Links: GM app page, career sim page, /sports/basketball/ once, cornerstone basketball-draft-gm-guide, 2 more published articles whose described content was confirmed, category page; no /tools/ link. Similarity max 0.011; preflight clean; dry run's only complaint is the missing review log.

Verified on 2026-10-02: NBA.com 2026 Play-In explainer (7 hosts 8, winner is the 7 seed; 9 hosts 10, loser out; 7-8 loser hosts 9-10 winner for the 8 seed; seeds 1-6 qualify directly); NBA PR 17 Nov 2020 (quote 'with the seventh-highest through the tenth-highest winning percentages in each conference' verbatim; 7/8 get two chances, 9/10 must win twice); AP report on NBA.com, July 2022 (owners' vote, 'a full-time path to the playoffs' verbatim, 2020 bubble play-in element); NBA.com 2002-03 review ('expanded from best-of-five to a best-of-seven' verbatim); NBA PR 23 Oct 2013 (2-3-2 'over the previous 29 seasons' hosting 1, 2, 6, 7; 2-2-1-1-1 from the 2014 Finals; 'aligns The Finals format with every other round' verbatim; used 1957-84 except 1978; travel/technology rationale); NBA.com key dates 2026-27 (season ends 11 April 2027, Play-In 13-16 April, playoffs from 17 April); 2026 playoffs schedule page (four rounds, series to four wins); NBA release of 28 May 2026 on the 3-2-1 Lottery (full text read: 14 to 16 teams; 3 balls for non-postseason teams, three worst records 'draft relegated' to 2 with a No. 12 floor, others can fall to No. 16; No. 9/10 seeds 2; 7-v-8 losers 1; first 16 picks drawn; consecutive No. 1 / three-straight top-five limits on a team's own pick even if traded; 2027-2029 drafts only). Corrections: Play-In is always three games per conference (was 'up to three'); 'fourth- to tenth-worst' replaced (non-postseason teams are set by conference seeding, not league rank); the writer's inference that the eventual No. 8 seed keeps lottery balls was cut and the case is now labelled as not specified by the league (body bullet and FAQ); first-pick chances kept only as labelled arithmetic with formula and inputs (7x3 + 3x2 + 4x2 + 2x1 = 37 balls; 3/37 = 8.1%, 2/37 = 5.4%, 1/37 = 2.7%) and stated assumptions (first ball decides No. 1, equal chance per ball, no restriction applies), no odds for later picks; added that pick limits follow a traded pick; 'in NBA.com's words' attributed to the AP report; the 2-3-2 rationale now quotes the release ('largely do not exist anymore'); app paragraph no longer asserts how the app's model works. App claims match dump-catalog (82-game season, playoff race, contracts, trades, rotations); not called fictional. Links: app, hub once, cornerstone, 2 published related, category; no /tools/ link. Similarity max 0.012; preflight clean; dry run's only complaint is the missing review log.

Verified on 2026-10-02 against the NBA's 30 June 2026 release (pr.nba.com and nba.com: cap $164.961m, tax $200.428m, minimum team salary $148.465m, aprons $209.015m/$221.686m, NT-MLE $15.044m, T-MLE $6.064m, room MLE $9.366m; effective 12:01 a.m. ET 1 July) and the NBA's CBA 101 (Nov 2024): term 2023-24 to 2029-30; cap = 44.74% of projected BRI minus benefits / 30, other levels move at the cap's rate, no level falls or rises over 10%; minimum-team-salary shortfall paid to players; tax on Tax Team Salary on the last day of the regular season with 2025-26+ rates $1.00/$1.25/$3.50/$4.75 then +$0.50, repeater = taxpayer in 4 of 5 seasons, +$2.00; 2024-25 bracket $5.168m growing with the cap; apron table rows A-J (first: BAE, NT-MLE, sign-and-trade, waived player paid above NT-MLE, expanded TPE; second: prior-year TPE, aggregation, cash, sign-and-trade TPE, T-MLE) and the hard-cap and T-MLE interaction; frozen pick (seventh draft; 2 of next 4 seasons moves it to the end of the round; 3 of 4 at or below releases it); Bird/Early Bird (175% or 105% of average, 2+ years)/Non-Bird (120%); 8% vs 5% raises; 5- vs 4-year lengths; MLE/BAE lengths and 2024-25 trade/waiver use; below-cap rule; roster 14-15, 12-13 for two weeks at a time and 28 days; two-way: three per team, 1-2 seasons, 50% of the zero-year minimum, 50 games, postseason only if converted before the last regular-season game. NBPA page confirmed as the host of the 2023 CBA PDF. Recomputed: gaps $35.467m/$8.587m/$12.671m; cap growth 164.961/140.588 = 1.1734 (17.3%); scaled 2024-25 tax 170.814 x 1.1734 = $200.427m vs $200.428m; tax bracket 5.168 x 1.1734 = $6.064m (formula now shown, labelled as not stated in the release); worked tax example 6.064x1.00 + 6.064x1.25 + 2.872x3.50 = $23.696m and repeater 6.064x3.00 + 6.064x3.25 + 2.872x5.50 = $53.696m. Corrections: the expanded TPE was described as letting a team take back 'at least 125%' of outgoing salary - rewritten to the CBA's rule (up to 200% plus $250,000 on small deals, tapering to 125% plus $250,000); '17.3% ... within the two-year limit' clarified (two 10% rises would allow 21%); dangling 'gets its own explanation' replaced with the actual first-apron matching rule (no $250,000 allowance, 100% back); FAQ now says the cap is set from projected revenue and other levels follow it; app paragraph no longer asserts how the game's own budget works. App claims match dump-catalog (Salary Cap Draft among eight formats; GM Mode covers contracts and trades); not called fictional. Links: app, hub once, cornerstone, 3 published related, category; no /tools/ link. Similarity max 0.025 (with nba-trade-rules); preflight clean; dry run's only complaint is the missing review log.

Verified on 2026-10-02 against the NBA's CBA 101 (Nov 2024): TPE table (standard/aggregated 100% + $250,000; expanded = greater of lesser of 200% + $250,000 and 100% + $7.752m (2024-25, indexed to the cap) and 125% + $250,000; room + $250,000), $250,000 allowance falls to zero above the first apron, expanded TPE a first-apron transaction, aggregated TPE / prior-year TPE / cash / sign-and-trade TPE second-apron transactions; two-month aggregation rule with the 16 December deadline-day exception and the three-or-more minimum-contract rule outside 15 December-deadline; sign-and-trade conditions (finished season on roster, 3-4 years, first year protected, before the regular season, not NT-MLE or room MLE; first-apron hard cap); extension-and-trade six-month block; cash limit $7.24m (2024-25), indexed, not netted; one-year Bird consent rule; waiting periods (rookies and two-way 30 days; free agents later of 3 months and 15 December; Bird/Early Bird over 120% of prior salary with team over the cap: 15 January); waived-player re-sign bar; frozen pick. Also the NBA's 30 June 2026 cap release (cap and apron figures), the 28 May 2026 lottery release (no top-12 to top-15 protections on newly traded picks; consecutive No. 1 / top-five limits; 2027-2029 drafts) and NBA.com key dates (2026-27 trade deadline 11 February). NBPA page hosts the 2023 CBA. Recomputed: cap growth 164.961/140.588 = 1.17336; cushion 7.752 x 1.17336 = $9.096m and cash limit 7.24 x 1.17336 = $8.495m (formulas now shown, labelled as our arithmetic); matching table $5m -> 10.25, $10m -> 19.096, $20m -> 29.096, $40m -> 50.25; switch-overs 8.846 and 35.384. Corrections: 'more than a 120% raise' (wrong - the rule is salary above 120% of the prior salary) fixed in the table and FAQ; draft-pick section no longer implies the two limits listed are the only pick-trading limits; 'currency of most rebuilding trades' softened (unsupported); football draft-order link anchor made accurate; app paragraph no longer asserts how the game's own rules work. App claims match dump-catalog (trades, contracts and rotations in GM Mode); not called fictional. Links: app, hub once, cornerstone, 3 published related, category; no /tools/ link. Similarity max 0.026 (with nba-apron-explained; different intent: legality checklist vs threshold ladder); preflight clean; dry run's only complaint is the missing review log.

Verified on 2026-10-02 against the full 2023 CBA text (NBPA-hosted PDF), Article X: s1(a) eligible for at least one draft / no more than two drafts; s1(b)(i) age 19 in the draft's calendar year and one NBA season since high-school graduation (or the class's) for non-international players; routes (ii)(A)-(G) checked row by row against the table; s1(c) international-player definition (three years' residence abroad while playing, never enrolled in a US college, did not finish US high school); s1(d) non-NBA professional contract ('in excess of a stipend for living expenses'); s2 draft before 10 July; s3 two rounds of team-count picks; s4 required tender by 15 July (first round) / 5 August (second round, 2024+ drafts), rights lapse at the next draft, rookie free agency 16 July / 6 August; s6(b) early-entry player who returns to college; s8(c) withdrawal notice received 10 days before the draft, no more than two withdrawals; s9 combine non-participation makes a player ineligible and an early-entry player deemed withdrawn. CBA 101 quotes ('at least 19 years old by the end of the calendar year of the Draft', 'at least one year removed from high school') verbatim; term 2023-24 to 2029-30. Lottery release (3-2-1 Lottery from the 2027 draft, 14 to 16 teams). Correction: the article said the league had scheduled the 2027 lottery for 10 May and the draft for 23-24 June - those are the 2026 dates on NBA.com's key-dates page, which does not yet list 2027 lottery or draft dates; replaced with that fact. Added the missing cornerstone link (basketball-draft-gm-guide, also added to relatedArticles); football draft-order anchor made accurate; career-sim paragraph no longer asserts how the app's draft works beyond the catalog (fictional simulation; stages youth to pro). No players named. App claims match dump-catalog for both apps; GM app not called fictional. Links: both app pages, hub once, cornerstone, 4 published related, category; no /tools/ link. Editions confirmed on 2026-10-02: official.nba.com still links the '2025-26 NBA Rulebook' (no 2026-27 rule changes on official.nba.com or pr.nba.com; 2026-27 Points of Emphasis/Areas of Focus are video posts), and FIBA's Official Basketball Rules 2026 v1.1 (approved by the Central Board 23 April 2026, valid as of 1 October 2026; assets.fiba.basketball) - the article states both editions. Every rule checked against the 2025-26 NBA Official Rules PDF and the FIBA 2026 PDF: NBA Rule 1-I(d) (23'9" arc, lines 3' from sidelines = 22 ft corners), 3-I (six fouls), 4-III (gather), 5-I(c) (three-point foot rules), 5-I(g) (tapped-in free throw = 2), 5-II (12-minute periods, 5-minute OT, 15-minute half), 5-V(b) (clock stops after baskets), timeouts (7 + 2 per OT; requested by a player in the game or the head coach), 7-II(d) and 7-IV(d) (rim contact; 14-second reset), 8/10-III (five-second throw-in, run the end line), 10-II (double dribble, carry), 10-VI/VII (offensive and defensive three seconds, arm's length, technical foul and possession), 10-VIII/IX, 10-XIII (two steps, first-step definition, hop), 10-XVI (five-second back-to-the-basket), 11-I (cylinder, downward flight), 12B-V (four team fouls then two shots, late-period allowance, three in OT); FIBA Art. 2.5.4 (6.75 m arc, 0.90 m corners, line in the 2-point area), 8.1/8.4/8.7, 16.2.1 (tipped last free throw = 2), 17 (5 s throw-in), 18 (head coach or first assistant only; 2/3/1 time-outs), 24.1.3 (no step limit while dribbling), 24.2 (2026 wording), 25.2 (two steps, same foot twice), 26, 27 (closely guarded 5 s), 28, 29 (rim contact; 14-second reset), 31 (restrictions end when the ball touches the ring; basket interference), 37 (new disruptive foul), 41.1 (five fouls), 42 (penalty after four team fouls). Recomputed the possession walk-through against those rules. Edits: four unsupported frequency claims softened ('most of the arguments', 'surprises people every season', 'most of the walk complaints', 'almost every whistle'); the tip-in point now says it applies in both books. App claims match dump-catalog (Career Sim is fictional; Live Sim shoot/pass, lock down/call for help). Links: career-sim app (primary), hub once, cornerstone, 3 published related, blog category; no /tools/ link. Similarity max 0.020 (with nba-vs-fiba-rules, which owns the side-by-side comparison; this article only summarises); preflight clean; dry run's only complaint is the missing review log.

Editions: NBA Official Rules 2025-26 (still the posted rulebook on 2026-10-02) and FIBA Official Basketball Rules 2026 v1.1 (valid from 1 October 2026), both stated. NBA checked: 3-I (six fouls), 12B-I (hold/push/charge/impede list; no team foul on offensive fouls; clear path two shots + ball; transition take one shot by any player in the game + ball), 4-IV(i) (take foul not in the last two minutes of the fourth or OT), 12B-IV (Flagrant 1 'unnecessary', Flagrant 2 'unnecessary and excessive', two shots + ball, ejection for F2 or two F1s, replay review required), 12B-V (four team fouls, two shots from the fifth, late allowance, three in OT), 12A-V (max two unsportsmanlike technicals then ejection; delay, defensive three seconds and flopping not unsportsmanlike; possession kept; one free throw; ejection for punching/fighting), 10-XVII (flopping technical), Comments on the Rules (4-foot restricted arc, secondary defender, path to the rim). FIBA 2026 checked: verticality/cylinder principle, initial legal guarding position (facing, both feet), charge/block principles (torso contact), time and distance (never less than one normal step), 2.5.7 and the no-charge rule (1.30 m; airborne shooter or passer), 36 (category 1/2 technical, 'shall be charged as a player foul' verbatim, one free throw), 37 (disruptive), 38 (flagrant), 39 (disqualifying foul/violence), 41 (five fouls; GD combinations), 42 (team foul definition incl. offensive fouls, penalty after four, OT counts as fourth quarter); rule-changes summary ('overly strict' verbatim). NBA 2026-27 Areas of Focus page: topics 'Flopping and Closeouts on Jump Shots - Landing Space' and 'Game Administration' - the article's mention matches. Worked example checked on Basketball-Reference's league-averages page (2025-26: FT% .783, ORtg 115.7): 2 x 0.783 = 1.566; 115.7/100 = 1.157; difference 0.409; 48/6 = 40/5 = 8 minutes; 36/3 = 12 and 30/2 = 15. Edits: three unsupported generalisations softened ('most confusion', 'almost every foul situation', 'the one fans argue about most'). App claims match dump-catalog (fictional career; Live Sim lock-down/call-for-help); article says nothing about how the game scores contact. Links: career-sim app, hub once, cornerstone, 3 published related, category; no /tools/ link. Similarity max 0.015; preflight clean; dry run's only complaint is the missing review log.

Every rule number in the comparison table checked on 2026-10-02 against the NBA Official Rules 2025-26 (still the posted edition) and FIBA Official Basketball Rules 2026 v1.1 (valid from 1 October 2026): NBA Rule 5-II (12-minute periods), court diagram (LENGTH 94 FEET, WIDTH 50 FEET, 22 FEET corner, 16 FEET lane), 1-I(d) (23'9"), 1-I(i) and Comments on the Rules II(C) Block-Charge (4-foot restricted arc, secondary defender), 3-I(a) (six fouls), 10-VII, 11, 5-VI (7 timeouts, 2 per OT; player in the game or head coach may request; 28-foot advance option), 6-VI (held ball: jump ball between the two players at the nearest circle), 14 (one challenge, second if successful; three challengeable events; timeout normally required; goaltending not challengeable in the last two minutes), 7-IV, 10-XIII, 10-VIII/IX, 12B-V, 12B-I/IV and 4-IV(i) (take, clear-path and flagrant penalties), 12A-V (flop technical not unsportsmanlike); FIBA Art. 2.1 (28 x 15 m), 2.5.3 (restricted area edges 2.45 m from mid-endline = 4.90 m), 2.5.4 (6.75 m, 0.90 m), 2.5.7 and 33.10 (1.30 m no-charge), 8.1, 12 (alternating possession), 18.2.5 and 18.3.1, 25, 26 (attackers only), 28, 29, 30, 31.2.3, 36-38 (category 1/2 technicals, disruptive, flagrant), 41.1, 42, 15.1 (act of shooting, frontcourt requirement with end-of-clock exception), Appendix F.4 (one head coach's challenge regardless of outcome, any time); rule-changes summary quote ('manipulating situations to create shooting fouls') verbatim. Recomputed conversions: 94 ft = 28.65 m, 50 ft = 15.24 m, 23'9" = 7.239 m, 22 ft = 6.706 m, 4 ft = 1.219 m, 16 ft = 4.877 m; arc gap 0.489 m; corner saving 0.533 m (NBA) vs 6.75 - (7.5 - 0.90) = 0.15 m (FIBA); 48/40 = 1.2; 240 vs 200 player-minutes; foul-rate arithmetic (8, 12, 15 minutes). Edits: the NBA challenge sentence now notes the last-two-minutes goaltending exception and that a timeout is 'normally' required (not when a mandatory or opposing timeout is under way); 'Our games are not governed by either rulebook' (an app claim not in the catalog) replaced with a statement about the article. App claims match dump-catalog (career sim fictional; GM app 82-game season, not called fictional). Links: both app pages, hub once, cornerstone, 3 published related (balanced-roster article confirmed to cover the minutes budget), blog category; no /tools/ link. Similarity max 0.020 (with basketball-rules-for-beginners, which only summarises the differences); preflight clean; dry run's only complaint is the missing review log.

Rules verified on 2026-10-02: NBA Official Rules 2025-26 (current posted edition) Rule 4-X (screen definition; quote 'delays or prevents an opponent from reaching a desired position' verbatim), 12B-III (normal step from an unaware stationary opponent; moving opponent one to two normal steps depending on speed; no lateral or forward movement after a legal position; may move in the same direction and path), 10-VII (defensive three seconds: arm's length, guarding position, exception while guarding the ball, must guard or exit after a pass); FIBA Official Basketball Rules 2026 Art. 33.7 (stationary inside the cylinder, both feet on the court; one normal step outside the field of vision; 1-2 normal steps against a moving opponent; moving screener illegal) and 26 (no defensive three seconds). NBA 2026-27 Points of Emphasis page (29 Sept 2026) read: its text only names video topics ('Off-Arm Push Offs by Offensive Players and Freedom of Movement - Screens'; 'Freedom of Movement - Perimeter & Post and Straight-Line Pathway Plays'). Correction: the article interpreted those topics as meaning moving screens and push-offs are 'under scrutiny this season' - cut and reduced to the topic titles the page states. Other edits: the FAQ attributed 'both feet on the floor' to both rulebooks - only FIBA says it; now attributed correctly with the NBA's own screening restriction; takeaway on defensive three seconds now says 'for more than three seconds'; 'five come up everywhere' (unsupported) softened. Coverage descriptions (drop, switch, hedge, blitz, ice) are explanatory tactics with no numbers or rule claims. App claims match dump-catalog (GM app: draft, rotations, own ratings and simulation, not called fictional; Career Sim: fictional, shoot/pass and lock-down/help decisions). Links: both app pages, hub once, cornerstone, 3 published related (positions article confirmed to cover screening bigs), category; no /tools/ link. Similarity max 0.017; preflight clean; dry run's only complaint is the missing review log.

FIBA Official Basketball Rules 2026 Art. 26 (three-second restriction applies only to the team in control). Zone shapes, soft spots and switching reasons are explanatory tactics with no numbers or rule claims. Edits: the article never said which rulebook editions it used - now names the NBA 2025-26 rulebook (latest posted as of October 2026) and FIBA's 2026 edition (valid from 1 October 2026); 'says so in as many words' overstated what the rule text says - reworded to quote it; 'narrower than many fans think' and 'Most teams mix the two' (unsupported) softened. App claims match dump-catalog (GM app: draft board, roster, own simulation of the season, not called fictional; Career Sim: fictional, lock-down/call-for-help). Links: both app pages, hub once, cornerstone, 3 published related (roster article confirmed to list rim protection, rebounding and perimeter defence as jobs), category; no /tools/ link. Every league figure recomputed on 2026-10-02 from Basketball-Reference's NBA League Averages (per game, regular season) table: 3PA per team-game 2.8/6.6/13.7/18.1/22.4/34.1/37.0 and 3P% .280/.331/.353/.355/.350/.358/.360 for 1979-80, 1989-90, 1999-00, 2009-10, 2014-15, 2019-20, 2025-26; share of shots from three = 3PA/FGA = 3.1/7.6/16.7/22.2/26.8/38.4/41.5% (table's 'about' figures match); pace 103.1 (1979-80), 93.9 (2014-15), 99.4 (2025-26); 2025-26 two-point % = (42.0 - 13.3)/(89.1 - 37.0) = 55.1%, worth 1.10 per attempt vs 3 x .360 = 1.08. Shot-value arithmetic checked (3 x 0.36 = 2 x 0.54 = 1.08; 1.5x rule; 35% = 52.5%, 40% = 60%). Glossary quotes verified verbatim (eFG% 'adjusts for the fact that a 3-point field goal is worth one more point than a 2-point field goal'; pace 'an estimate of the number of possessions per 48 minutes by a team'); NBA.com 1979-80 season review quote ('a popular facet of the ABA game') verbatim. Rules checked in the NBA Official Rules 2025-26: 10-VII(c) ('The defenders may double-team any player'), 10-VI (offensive three seconds), 10-XVI (five-second back-to-the-basket), 7 (24-second clock). Edit: the article cited NBA rules without naming an edition - now says 2025-26 (latest posted) at both rule references. System descriptions are explanatory tactics with no numbers. Links: both app pages, hub once, cornerstone, 3 published related, category; no /tools/ link. Similarity max 0.020; preflight clean; dry run's only complaint is the missing review log.

Verified on 2026-10-02: Basketball-Reference glossary definitions (Usg% 'percentage of team plays used by a player while he was on the floor', AST% 'percentage of teammate field goals a player assisted', ORB/DRB/TRB% shares of available rebounds) match the article's paraphrases; BPM 2.0 page by its developer Daniel Myers contains the quote 'on defense the box score is quite limited' verbatim; NBA Official Rules 2025-26 (current posted edition) Rule 1-I(d) and court diagram (23'9" arc, lines 3 ft from the sidelines = 22 ft corners), Comments on the Rules II(C) (4-foot restricted arc, secondary defender, path directly to the rim), 10-VII (defensive three seconds); FIBA Official Basketball Rules 2026 Art. 2.5.4 (6.75 m; 0.90 m corner lines -> 7.5 - 0.90 = 6.60 m, our arithmetic), 33.2 principle of verticality ('must not be penalised' verbatim), 26 (no defensive three seconds). GM app: pool built from real players' careers with the game's own ratings per content-spec rule 10; 'balance and depth carry more weight than any single marquee pick' from its description; not called fictional; no player data reproduced).
